wins: Maintained high reward (57.5) despite single episode, indicating consistent progressive steps through initial reconnaissance and enumeration.
Engaged mentor support 15 times, allowing rapid adjustments during complex phases.
fails: Zero percent success rate; attack never reached final objective due to inability to pivot from enumeration to exploitation.
Frequent stalls around credential validation and exploitation steps, suggesting missing tactics for privilege escalation.
key_outcomes.summary: Strong reconnaissance discipline yielded high reward, but lack of effective exploitation and persistence actions prevented successful mission completion.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Failure to transition from service enumeration to successful exploitation; sessions repeatedly stalled after banner grabbing and port mapping.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH service banner captured
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted SSH scripts (banner, bruteforce checks) via nmap and record credentials/banners

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80/443 responds with web service
skill_cards.then_action: Execute gobuster with common directories + nikto for web-level vulnerabilities

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP forms or SSH prompts appear after enumeration
skill_cards.then_action: Search harvested banners/logs for credential patterns and test default creds with hydra

memory_ops.reason: Consistent success in capturing banners and building metadata for attack surface
Reliable enumeration of web assets enabled further payload planning

next_experiments.title: Automate exploitation handoff after enumeration
next_experiments.description: After wiki or SSH service enumeration completes, immediately run matched exploit modules (e.g., Metasploit's auxiliary/scanner/ssh/ssh_login) to reduce manual delay between recon and exploitation.

next_experiments.title: Integrate credential harvesting with brute-force loops
next_experiments.description: Feed collected banners and known defaults into hydra/medusa iteratively to improve success in breaking authentication gates identified during enumeration.
